players.product: Sqale neutral-atom quantum computer (plus quantum clocks and RF sensors)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Kinsella: Infleqtion's gate fidelities have risen from somewhere in the 50% range in 2018 to 99.73% now, on par with other modalities such as superconducting; it holds the record of 1,600 physical qubits on its machine in Boulder; its logical-qubit roadmap goes from 12 at the end of last year to 30 at the end of this year and 100 by the end of 2028, the level at which he expects useful applications versus classical computers.
quarterly_data.figure: gate fidelity 99.73%; 30 logical qubits at the end of this year; 100 by the end of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Kinsella: Infleqtion has sold three quantum computers - one to the state of Illinois, one to the United Kingdom and one to the Institute for Molecular Science in Japan - with a number of other opportunities in the pipeline.

CEO Matt Kinsella: NASA awarded Infleqtion an expansion of its contract of $20 million, bringing it to over $40 million cumulatively, to put a quantum gravity gradiometer (two Bose-Einstein condensate sensors side by side in a satellite) into space to track changes in gravity on the Earth's surface.
quarterly_data.figure: $20 million contract expansion; over $40 million cumulatively

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Kinsella: Infleqtion manufactures its own ultra-high vacuum cells and builds its technologies internally, procuring lasers and photonic systems on the open market - in many cases from smaller vendors of bespoke lab-grade photonics rather than traditional data-center / telecom photonic vendors such as Lumentum, because rubidium and cesium atoms use different wavelengths - and is increasingly bringing these in-house as chip-scale integrated photonics; the supply chain is functioning quite well; it is debating whether to use contract manufacturers for final assembly of its clocks.

CEO Matt Kinsella: about a year ago Infleqtion worked with NVIDIA on the Anderson impurity model, with pre-processing on GPUs and electron modelling sent to logical qubits on Infleqtion's quantum computer; he describes NVIDIA's role as an industry enabler through its chips, Ising models and NVQLink, and calls it a wonderful partnership.

CEO Matt Kinsella: some Infleqtion technologies fall under export controls (some on the ITAR list); it cannot sell to Iran or China, but there have been no restrictions of substance on its products to U.S. allies so far and he does not anticipate any.
